results.input: MetaGPT’s original role-based, SOP-driven multi-agent thesis and the current official MetaGPT documentation or repository. Focus on what is durable, what assumptions it makes, and limits of a single prompt.

output.authoritative_sources: [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352) | [MetaGPT Official Documentation](https://docs.deepwisdom.ai/main/en/guide/get_started/introduction.html)
output.design_recommendations: Adopt a role-based architecture that mandates the creation of structured intermediate artifacts to maintain a durable "truth" across agent handoffs. Embed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into the communication protocol to ensure agents adhere to verifiable state transitions. Implement a global message bus using a "watch" mechanism to decouple individual agent logic from the overall system orchestration. Require executive feedback loops that execute and validate agent outputs against success criteria before proceeding to downstream tasks. Establish clear boundaries for autonomous execution by requiring human checkpoints for high-ambiguity or large-scale strategic decisions.
output.research_lane: MetaGPT’s original role-based, SOP-driven multi-agent thesis and the current official MetaGPT documentation or repository.
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single launch prompt can realistically initiate a full software development lifecycle for small-to-medium projects, producing a complete package from requirements to unit-tested code (https://docs.deepwisdom.ai/main/en/guide/get_started/introduction.html). Initialization is limited by the framework's assumption of a pre-defined "assembly line" SOP, making it brittle when applied to ambiguous tasks that lack established domain-specific procedures (https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352). Large-scale projects exceeding ~2000 lines of code or those requiring iterative human-in-the-loop adjustments cannot be responsibly handled by a single prompt without risking logical inconsistencies (https://github.com/geekan/MetaGPT/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md).
output.verified_findings: MetaGPT implements a meta-programming mechanism that encodes human Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) into structured prompt sequences to guide LLM-based agent collaboration (https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352). The framework utilizes role-based specialization, where agents generate mandatory structured artifacts such as PRDs and design documents to reduce cascading hallucinations (https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352). A centralized environment facilitates communication through a "watch-and-publish" mechanism, allowing agents to observe specific message types and trigger corresponding actions asynchronously (https://docs.deepwisdom.ai/main/en/guide/tutorials/concepts.html). MetaGPT claims a significant improvement in task completion rates and code quality by integrating an executive feedback mechanism that performs runtime debugging and execution (https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352).

results.input: Current official guidance on multi-agent orchestration and agent evaluation from major agent-framework providers. Focus on centralized orchestration versus peer delegation, explicit handoffs, traces, evaluations, and human checkpoints.

output.authoritative_sources: [LangGraph: Multi-Agent Workflows](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/multi_agent/) | [Azure Architecture Center: AI Agent Orchestration Patterns](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/ai-ml/guide/ai-agent-design-patterns) | [Microsoft AutoGen: AgentEval Framework](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/0.2/blog/2024/06/21/AgentEval/) | [LangGraph: Human-in-the-loop Breakpoints](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/human_in_the_loop/breakpoints/) | [OpenAI Swarm: Orchestrating Agents](https://github.com/openai/swarm)
output.design_recommendations:
Adopt a hierarchical orchestration model for cross-functional tasks to maintain specialized security boundaries and reduce prompt complexity.
Integrate mandatory human-in-the-loop breakpoints for high-stakes decisions using persistent state checkpointers to ensure auditability.
Utilize automated evaluation agents to continuously monitor and validate agent performance against dynamic utility criteria.
Standardize state updates using independent reducer functions to maintain data integrity across concurrent agent operations.
Implement strict iteration limits and idempotent logic for all tool-using agents to mitigate the risk of infinite loops and state corruption.
output.research_lane: Current official guidance on multi-agent orchestration and agent evaluation from major agent-framework providers. Focus on centralized orchestration versus peer delegation, explicit handoffs, traces, evaluations, and human checkpoints.
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single prompt can responsibly initialize a static multi-agent pipeline or a simple conditional graph with predefined specialized roles and tool access. It cannot responsibly initiate high-stakes autonomous systems that lack explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, persistent state checkpointers, or multi-agent evaluation guardrails to prevent brittle behavior.
output.verified_findings:
Multi-agent systems utilize orchestration patterns ranging from sequential pipelines to dynamic peer delegation to handle tasks exceeding single-agent capabilities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/ai-ml/guide/ai-agent-design-patterns).
LangGraph models workflows as stateful graphs where nodes perform work and edges define transitions via message passing for reliable state management (https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/multi_agent/).
Human-in-the-loop oversight is enabled by dynamic interrupts that pause execution and surface payloads, requiring persistent checkpointers for state resumption (https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/human_in_the_loop/breakpoints/).
The AgentEval framework automates utility assessment by using specialized agents to generate, quantify, and verify evaluation criteria for LLM applications (https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/0.2/blog/2024/06/21/AgentEval/).
OpenAI Swarm emphasizes lightweight orchestration through explicit handoffs where agents return the next agent to be invoked, simplifying peer delegation (https://github.com/openai/swarm).

results.input: Knowledge-library architecture and retrieval: authoritative or original documentation for source-grounded retrieval, hierarchical or graph-based memory, provenance, filtered context loading, and avoiding a single monolithic prompt.

output.authoritative_sources: [GraphRAG Architecture - Microsoft Open Source](https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/architecture/) | [Structured Hierarchical Retrieval - LlamaIndex Documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/examples/query_engine/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/) | [GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM discovery on narrative private data - Microsoft Research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-unlocking-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/)
output.design_recommendations: Implement a multi-level indexing strategy that generates concise metadata summaries for individual documents and aggregate community summaries for thematic clusters. Enforce strict provenance tracking by requiring every retrieved context chunk to carry a unique identifier linked to its primary source URL. Use auto-retrieval filters to dynamically prune the context window, ensuring that only metadata-validated chunks are passed to the final synthesis prompt. Replace monolithic synthesis prompts with a modular chain consisting of query intent classification, filtered retrieval, and evidence-based grounding. Deploy LLM caching at the workflow level to maintain idempotency and reduce latency during complex graph traversals.
output.research_lane: Knowledge-library architecture and retrieval: authoritative or original documentation for source-grounded retrieval, hierarchical or graph-based memory, provenance, filtered context loading, and avoiding a single monolithic prompt.
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single launch prompt can responsibly initiate a query transformation and routing process that selects which hierarchical index or community summary to target. It cannot responsibly perform the initial knowledge graph extraction or hierarchical indexing, which requires a multi-pass, asynchronous data pipeline to ensure structural integrity. The launch prompt must be restricted to orchestrating the retrieval of pre-processed summaries rather than attempting to ingest raw, un-indexed corpora in one step.
output.verified_findings: GraphRAG organizes unstructured text into a structured hierarchy of entities, relationships, and community summaries to improve retrieval for complex, cross-document queries (https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/architecture/). Hierarchical retrieval systems use IndexNodes and metadata filters to dynamically select relevant documents before content extraction, replacing flat vector search (https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/examples/query_engine/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/). Provenance is maintained by mapping graph entities and relationships directly back to their original source document chunks for verifiable grounding (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-unlocking-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/). Multi-stage retrieval pipelines avoid monolithic prompts by decomposing queries into sub-tasks including intent classification and targeted context loading (https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/examples/query_engine/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/multi_doc_auto_retrieval/). Context loading is optimized through community-level summarization, allowing reasoning over large-scale datasets without exceeding context window limits (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-unlocking-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/).

results.input: Current product-discovery, specification-driven development, and MVP practice. Focus on needs analysis, assumption testing, PRD/SRS separation, measurable outcomes, and convergence between specification and implementation.

output.authoritative_sources: [Silicon Valley Product Group (SVPG) - Discovery vs Delivery](https://svpg.com/discovery-delivery/) | [Jama Software - Product Requirements Document (PRD) Guide](https://www.jamasoftware.com/requirements-management-guide/writing-requirements/product-requirements-document/) | [Augment - What is Spec-Driven Development?](https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/what-is-spec-driven-development)
output.design_recommendations: Mandate the use of Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax (EARS) for all agent-generated specifications to ensure measurable outcomes. | Establish a 'Product Trio' agent configuration consisting of PM, Designer, and Engineer roles to maintain continuous discovery-delivery integration. | Implement automated traceability mapping between Product Requirements (PRD) and Software Specifications (SRS) to prevent scope drift. | Utilize executable specifications as binding contracts that constrain implementation and facilitate automated verification. | Require explicit assumption logging and prioritization for all MVP initiatives to guide systematic testing cycles.
output.research_lane: Current product-discovery, specification-driven development, and MVP practice. Focus on needs analysis, assumption testing, PRD/SRS separation, measurable outcomes, and convergence between specification and implementation.
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single prompt can responsibly generate a structured PRD draft and initial assumption log from high-level business objectives. It cannot responsibly perform real-world assumption testing or ensure cross-functional alignment without iterative human-in-the-loop feedback and external market data.
output.verified_findings: Product discovery is a continuous activity aimed at uncovering value-creating solutions, distinct from delivery which focuses on producing those solutions (https://svpg.com/discovery-delivery/). Technical requirements in a PRD must be measurable, using specific thresholds rather than qualitative terms to ensure testability (https://www.jamasoftware.com/requirements-management-guide/writing-requirements/product-requirements-document/). A clear separation between PRD (what) and SRS (how) is essential to maintain traceability and avoid implementation-level details in high-level requirements (https://www.jamasoftware.com/requirements-management-guide/writing-requirements/product-requirements-document/). Spec-driven development (SDD) treats specifications as executable contracts that constrain implementation and ensure convergence through automated verification (https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/what-is-spec-driven-development). Continuous discovery habits require weekly customer interactions by a 'Product Trio' to validate assumptions and mitigate risks early (https://www.productcompass.pm/p/product-discovery-sources-of-insights).

results.input: Governance and risk management for AI-enabled systems. Focus on human oversight, decision rights, auditability, safety boundaries, model/agent evaluation, and controlled change management.

output.authoritative_sources: [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) | [EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Official Text)](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/)
output.design_recommendations: Implement a mandatory human-in-the-loop verification protocol for all agent actions classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act framework. Integrate an instantaneous deactivation mechanism or 'kill switch' that triggers if agent performance deviates from predefined safety boundaries. Automate the generation of immutable audit logs for every agent decision and human intervention to ensure full traceability. Establish a centralized governance registry that maps specific agent roles to restricted decision rights and required oversight levels. Conduct regular automated red-teaming exercises to stress-test safety guardrails against foreseeable misuse and model drift.
output.research_lane: Governance and risk management for AI-enabled systems
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single prompt can responsibly initialize baseline risk assessments, draft organizational governance policies, and configure automated monitoring triggers for known failure modes. It cannot responsibly grant autonomous decision-making authority for high-risk tasks, bypass mandatory human oversight requirements, or finalize legal compliance certifications without multi-stakeholder validation.
output.verified_findings: Risk management must be a continuous, iterative process throughout the entire AI lifecycle, encompassing identification, estimation, and evaluation of foreseeable risks (https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/9/). High-risk AI systems require human oversight designed into the system to allow natural persons to override, stop, or ignore AI outputs (https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/14/). Governance functions must establish clear organizational risk tolerance, assigned roles, and accountability mechanisms for AI actors (https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/govern/). Safety boundaries require active mechanisms to supersede or deactivate systems demonstrating performance inconsistent with intended use (https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/manage/). Post-deployment monitoring must include incident response, recovery plans, and controlled change management to sustain system trustworthiness (https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/manage/).

results.input: Living documentation, version control, and commercial operating systems. Focus on ADRs, docs-as-code, customer-research/sales/support feedback loops, and how operational evidence should update product and business decisions.

output.authoritative_sources: [Master architecture decision records (ADRs): Best practices for effective decision-making](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/master-architecture-decision-records-adrs-best-practices-for-effective-decision-making/) | [Docs as Code - Write the Docs](https://www.writethedocs.org/guide/docs-as-code/) | [Customer Feedback Loops: Do Them Right or Don’t Bother](https://productschool.com/blog/user-experience/customer-feedback-loop)
output.design_recommendations:
Implement a "blocking merge" policy in CI/CD pipelines to ensure no feature is deployed without accompanying documentation or updated ADRs.
Adopt a "readout" meeting style for ADRs where participants spend the first 15 minutes reading the document before discussing, ensuring focused and informed feedback.
Automate the collection of customer research and support tickets into a "Docs-as-Code" repository to trigger automated summaries for product decision-making.
Establish a "team law" status for ADRs, where superseded decisions are explicitly linked to new records to maintain a clear historical audit trail.
Use plain-text markup (Markdown) for all operational evidence to ensure it remains version-controlled and searchable alongside the codebase.
output.research_lane: Living documentation, version control, and commercial operating systems. Focus on ADRs, docs-as-code, customer-research/sales/support feedback loops, and how operational evidence should update product and business decisions.
output.single_prompt_boundary: A single prompt can responsibly initialize a documentation scaffold, such as generating a standard ADR template or a basic README from project metadata. However, it cannot autonomously finalize architectural decisions or close feedback loops without human validation of trade-offs and direct customer interaction. Prerequisites include a pre-configured version control repository and a defined governance structure for decision approval.
output.verified_findings:
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) capture the context, alternatives, and rationale behind technical choices, serving as a "team law" that fosters transparency and accountability (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/master-architecture-decision-records-adrs-best-practices-for-effective-decision-making/).
The "Docs-as-Code" methodology treats documentation as a first-class citizen by using version control, plain-text markup, and automated tests to integrate writers directly into development workflows (https://www.writethedocs.org/guide/docs-as-code/).
Effective customer feedback loops consist of four components—Ask, Listen, Act, and Follow-up—where the "Follow-up" stage is essential to close the loop and build long-term user trust (https://productschool.com/blog/user-experience/customer-feedback-loop).
Blocking the merging of new features that lack documentation is a primary mechanism used to incentivize developers to maintain living documentation (https://www.writethedocs.org/guide/docs-as-code/).
Streamlining decision-making requires cross-functional but lean participant lists and a focus on single, timely decisions to avoid prolonged discussion and repeated refactoring (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/master-architecture-decision-records-adrs-best-practices-for-effective-decision-making/).
